original_question: Problem 7.4 (S. Vũ Ngo.c). Define (and detect) the quantum Chern class.
target_in_paper: Section 7.1 (Quantum integrable systems), Problem 7.4 (S. Vũ Ngọc): "Define (and detect) the quantum Chern class."
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's official problem statement essentially verbatim and keeps the correct attribution to S. Vũ Ngọc. It also preserves the paper's two-part emphasis: one must both define the invariant and explain how to detect it.
missing_details: The paper means the quantum analogue of the classical Chern class of Duistermaat (also called the Duistermaat-Chern class), not an arbitrary Chern class from another context.
The ambient setting is a finite-dimensional quantum integrable system: n self-adjoint semiclassical operators P_1, ..., P_n on a quantum Hilbert space corresponding to a symplectic manifold M^{2n}.

The operators are assumed to commute exactly, [P_i, P_j] = 0, and to have principal symbols p_j = sigma(P_j) with almost everywhere independent differentials; this is the paper's notion of independence for the underlying classical system.
The classical invariant being quantized is the obstruction, together with Hamiltonian monodromy, to globalizing action-angle coordinates for the associated classical Lagrangian fibration.
The nearby paragraph explains what 'detect' is intended to mean: the invariant may or may not be visible in the semiclassical joint spectrum.
More specifically, the paper suggests that the quantum Chern class may instead appear as phase information carried by joint eigenfunctions.
The same paragraph also points to transversal 'shift operators' between neighboring joint eigenspaces as a likely mechanism for defining or detecting the invariant.
The problem is explicitly motivated by the preceding classical Problem 6.8, which asks for natural classical integrable systems with non-trivial Duistermaat-Chern class.

For context, the paper notes that the classical Chern class always vanishes in two degrees of freedom and that there are no known physically meaningful examples with non-trivial Chern class in three degrees of freedom; this explains why the question is subtle.
There are no ring, field, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency parameters here; the missing assumptions are geometric and semiclassical rather than algebraic.
refined_question: Let (P_1, ..., P_n) be a finite-dimensional quantum integrable system in the sense of Section 7.1: self-adjoint semiclassical operators on a quantum Hilbert space corresponding to a symplectic manifold M^{2n}, satisfying [P_i, P_j] = 0 and having principal symbols p_j = sigma(P_j) whose differentials are almost everywhere independent, so that p = (p_1, ..., p_n) defines a classical integrable system. Define a quantum analogue of the classical Chern (Duistermaat-Chern) class of the associated Lagrangian fibration—the classical obstruction, alongside Hamiltonian monodromy, to global action-angle coordinates—and determine how this quantum invariant can be detected from the quantum data, in particular whether it is encoded in the semiclassical joint spectrum or only in phase information of joint eigenfunctions, possibly via shift operators transversal to the Lagrangian fibration.
justification: The draft already captures the exact official target: Problem 7.4 is stated in the paper with exactly this wording. However, taken alone, it is not stand-alone. The paragraph immediately before Problem 7.4 identifies the intended classical source of the problem as the Chern or Duistermaat-Chern class from Problem 6.8, contrasts it with quantum monodromy, and says that unlike monodromy it may be invisible in the joint spectrum and instead appear as a phase on eigenfunctions, possibly through shift operators transversal to the Lagrangian fibration. Earlier in the same subsection, the paper fixes the ambient meaning of 'quantum integrable system' as n commuting self-adjoint semiclassical operators with almost everywhere independent principal symbols. The refined question restores exactly this context and no more, so it stays narrow and faithful to the paper rather than broadening the problem into unrelated Chern-class or general quantization questions.
